why: I compared each verifier check's PASS and FAIL conditions with the words of its expect line. Checks 3 and 4 stay close to their lines: Check 3 needs `--shout` plus text saying what it does, and Check 4 needs the live page to contain `--shout`. Check 1 adds an "exits 0" requirement that the line doesn't clearly require. Check 2 breaks the criterion clearly. Its line says only "without --shout the output is unchanged", but its PASS condition also requires "`npm test` passes", and its FAIL condition includes "failing `npm test`". A passing test suite isn't something those words force. Check 2 also compares exit codes, which goes beyond "output". These stricter tests belong under Advisory, but they sit inside the PASS/FAIL conditions.
